what: A photo in a screen-height section is visible only through a small elliptical window (14% wide · 30% tall, centered 40% from the top). The moment the top edge of the section passes the top edge of the screen, the window opens to ellipse(100% 100%) over .4s ease-out and fills the screen — scrolling back up closes it again. Then, from when the section has risen 70% above the screen until its bottom edge touches the bottom edge of the screen, the photo blurs from 0 → 16px bound to scroll (power1.out), with the photo’s 1s ease-out transition smoothly following the blur. On phone (767 and below) the closed window is 34% 28% at 50% 50%

duration.Overcast: Section top −70% → bottom bottom(scrub) + follows by 1s

options.from-narrow: Closed ellipse at 767px and below, base CSS ‹34% 28% at 50% 50%›
options.start: Start position (ScrollTrigger start), default top top
options.blur: End blur (px), default 16 — at 0 there is no blur
options.ease: Blur curve, default power1.out (the original gives no curve, so the GSAP default applies)
options.[data-fx-part=mask]: Panel cropped to an ellipse (child, fills the section height) — its first child is a photo that blurs

note: The original script sets the scrub range to start top top · end top 50%, so the end comes before the start — GSAP treats that range as zero length and jumps to the end value the moment it passes top top, with a CSS transition .4s bridging the gap. The part produces the same result with onEnter · onLeaveBack

from.where: index.html .hm-reveal (a viewport-height section after the principal’s intro) — original inline script animetion_sec: clip-path ellipse(14% 30% at 50% 40%) → ellipse(100% 100% at 50% 50%) · start top top · end top 50% · scrub, photo blur(16px) · start top -70% · end bottom bottom · scrub, photo transition all 1s ease-out. The mask has .animetion_sec--mask with transition all .4s ease-out written on it, but .page-animation-2 .scroll_active on the same element (transition all 2s ease, two-level specificity) wins, so the actual reveal is 2s ease.
